patch_description: Instead of a greedy construction with random sampling, I use an iterated local search / simulated-annealing style approach: start from a randomized ordering, then repeatedly try pairwise swaps and single-transaction reinsertions to reduce makespan, evaluated exactly via `get_opt_seq_cost`. A simple incremental evaluation (caching the current cost) keeps it fast, and multiple restarts with a time budget avoid bad local minima. This explores the permutation space much more broadly than greedy sampling and directly optimizes the true makespan.
